Selection regimes

Source: R/regimes.R
regimes.Rd

A simulation runs through a list of regimes:

Usage

drift(generations)

stabilizing(generations, omega, theta = NULL)

directional(generations, delta_theta, omega, theta = NULL)

fluctuating(
  generations,
  every,
  step,
  omega,
  structure = "correlated",
  bounds = c(-1, 1),
  theta = NULL
)

Arguments

generations

number of generations.

omega

fitness surface covariance matrix (traits x traits), or a single number w, meaning w times the identity.

theta

optimum at the start of the regime, or NULL.

delta_theta

change in the optimum per generation (vector, one value per trait).

every

number of generations between jumps of the optimum.

step

size of a jump (one value, or one per trait).

structure

"correlated", "independent" or a list of trait blocks.

bounds

lower and upper bound of the optimum (NULL for none).

Value

An evomod_regime object.

Details

  • drift(): no selection.

  • stabilizing(): Gaussian fitness surface with optimum theta and covariance omega, $$w(z) = \exp\left(-\frac{1}{2} (z - \theta)^\top \Omega^{-1} (z - \theta)\right).$$

  • directional(): as stabilizing, but the optimum moves by delta_theta every generation (before selection).

  • fluctuating(): as stabilizing, but after every every generations the optimum jumps by step up or down (do O & Whitlock 2023). With structure = "correlated" all traits jump in the same direction; with "independent" each trait draws its own direction; a list of trait blocks (e.g. list(1:2, 3:4)) makes traits jump together within blocks and independently between them (traits not in any block jump alone). A jump that would take a trait of the block outside bounds is not taken, so at a bound the optimum stays or moves inward with probability 1/2 each; bounds = NULL leaves the optimum unbounded.

When theta is NULL the regime starts from the optimum at the end of the previous regime (the origin for the first one).

Examples

regimes <- list(drift(100), stabilizing(1000, omega = 20),
                directional(1000, delta_theta = c(0.005, 0), omega = 20))
fluctuating(5000, every = 10, step = 0.2, omega = 1, structure = "correlated")
#> <evomod regime> fluctuating for 5000 generations
fluctuating(5000, every = 10, step = 0.2, omega = 1, structure = list(1:2, 3:4))
#> <evomod regime> fluctuating for 5000 generations
